summary: Correction round on top of attempt 1 (no production behavior changed). RC1 (TQ-11.3-1): strengthened ProviderReadsUseNoConditionalRequestRevisionTokenOrHistorySinceWatermark so the provider request set is pinned to an explicit allowlist of permitted reconciliation endpoint paths (/api/v3/system/status, /api/v3/movie, /api/v3/moviefile, /api/v3/series, /api/v3/episode, /api/v3/episodeFile) and permitted query-parameter names (movieId, seriesId, includeEpisodeFile, episodeFileIds), in addition to the existing conditional-header and literal history/since and h= exclusions, so an unnamed revision-token or history fetch fails the test. Sensitivity was proven with a temporary unlisted /api/v3/history?page=1 request that made the test fail (Failed 1), then reverted. RC2 (11.3-F3): corrected the task 11.3 changelog wording to say the reconciliation test covers PostScan, Scheduled, and PostSave (it iterates all three). RC3 (TQ-11.3-2): strengthened ReconciliationInvalidatesTheInventoryForEverySource to assert the seeded observation set is actually served before the reconciliation (TryGet true) and is no longer served after it (TryGet false), not only that Count drops to 0; the provider-level InvalidatedObservationSetIsRePopulatedOnTheNextRead test continues to cover re-population. Attempt 1's implementation is otherwise unchanged: the ArrTags-side invalidation surface (ArrInventoryCache.Invalidate/InvalidateAll and the ArrInventoryCacheProvider equivalents), the webhook, refresh/post-scan, scheduled/manual, and post-save reconciliation sources, the bounded TTL fallback, the unchanged periodic scheduled reconciliation, and the no-conditional-request/no-revision-token/no-history-since/no-SignalR constraint are all preserved; limitation F1 remains open (task 11.4 records it resolved).

known_limitations: In-flight population interaction: a single-flight population already in flight when an invalidation runs may complete afterwards and store the provider read it took before the invalidation. Consequence: that observation set can be served until its configured inventory TTL (StaleUntil), and it is discarded by the next webhook, refresh/post-scan, or scheduled/manual reconciliation; the cache is non-authoritative so correctness does not depend on it. This is the bounded behavior the task asked to document rather than fence with a generation counter.

Reconciliation invalidation runs after the no-enabled-provider and lifecycle-fence guards in ReconcileAsync, so a run that is skipped for no enabled provider or a raised fence does not invalidate. Consequence: no observation set is discarded for a run that enqueues no work; the next actual reconciliation, webhook, or the TTL still invalidates.

Webhook connection resolution uses ArrConnectionCatalog.FromSnapshot(current snapshot) by provider kind; because the catalog always returns both provider connections, the bounded invalidate-all fallback is defensive and is not exercised by the current catalog shape.

Limitation F1 is deliberately not recorded as resolved by this task; task 11.4 records it resolved after the Goal C integration verification. The live pinned-host verification of this behavior remains owned by task 14.3 per the project plan.
Validation is at the unit/integration-test level (no live Jellyfin or Arr host was run for this task).

The endpoint allowlist in the RC1 test pins the six documented reconciliation endpoints and the four documented selector query keys; a future legitimate provider endpoint added to the reads must be added to the allowlist, which is the intended behavior of the pin.
